title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 9th Congressional District
area: East-central and northeastern Pennsylvania, including Carbon, Columbia, Montour, Northumberland, Schuylkill, Sullivan, and Wyoming counties and parts of Luzerne County.

context.text: Dan Meuser was unopposed in the May 19, 2026 Republican primary. Rachel Wallace defeated Jennifer Brothers and Daniel Byron in the Democratic primary.

candidates.name: Dan Meuser
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2019); Chair, House Committee on Financial Services

summary.text: Dan Meuser is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Pennsylvania's 9th District, first elected in 2018. He chairs the House Committee on Financial Services and previously served as Pennsylvania Secretary of Revenue under Gov. Tom Corbett. Before public office, he was president of Pride Mobility Corporation, a motorized wheelchair manufacturer.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Cornell University in 1986.
Served as head of the Pennsylvania Department of Revenue from 2011 to 2015 under Gov. Tom Corbett (R).
Worked as president of Pride Mobility Corporation, a motorized wheelchair manufacturer, before entering public office.

priorities.text: Says he is committed to advancing the "America First agenda," including securing the border, promoting American energy dominance, growing the economy, and protecting national security.
priorities.quote: Working alongside President Trump and a unified Republican Congress, I am committed to advancing the America First agenda which the American people voted for.

priorities.text: Lists extending the 2017 Trump tax cuts, expanding small-business access to capital, and supporting domestic natural gas production among his priorities.

positions.summary: Supports reimplementing "Remain in Mexico," ending "Catch and Release," and ensuring Border Patrol agents have resources to stop illegal immigration, drugs, and human trafficking.
positions.quote: Securing the Border: Stop the flow of illegal immigrants, drugs, and human trafficking from coming across our border. Reimplement Remain in Mexico, end Catch and Release.

positions.summary: Supports extending the 2017 Trump tax cuts, including the small-business deduction and R&D tax credit, rather than raising taxes on businesses.
positions.quote: Supporting Small Businesses: Extend the Trump Tax Cuts and Jobs, including provisions like bonus depreciation, the small business deduction, and the R&D tax credit.

positions.summary: Prioritizes expanding domestic natural gas exploration and production over transitioning away from fossil fuels.
positions.quote: Unleashing Energy Dominance: Support domestic energy exploration and production, particularly of clean Pennsylvania natural gas, to lower costs for families, create good-paying jobs, and eliminate reliance on foreign adversaries for energy.

record.text: Chairs the Committee on Financial Services in the 2025-2026 Congress; also assigned to the Committee on Small Business.

candidates.name: Rachel Wallace
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19 Democratic primary unopposed by write-in-eligible opponents, defeating Jennifer Brothers and Daniel Byron

summary.text: Rachel Wallace is a Pottsville, Pennsylvania native who has worked for former Congressman Tim Holden, the U.S. State Department, the U.S. Senate, and the White House, where she served as Chief of Staff for the Office of Management and Budget. She is challenging incumbent Dan Meuser, campaigning on health care and lowering the cost of living.

background.text: Born and raised in Pottsville, Pennsylvania; graduate of Pottsville Area High School.

Began her career working for her home-district Congressman, Tim Holden, and went on to serve in the U.S. State Department, the U.S. Senate, and as Chief of Staff for the White House Office of Management and Budget.
Says she moved back to southern Schuylkill County, where her family has lived for 10 generations, to be closer to family after her mother was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease.

priorities.text: Says nearly 30,000 people in the district will lose health insurance because of Dan Meuser's votes, and that she will fight to save rural hospitals and end prior-authorization practices.
priorities.quote: Nearly 30,000 people in our part of Pennsylvania will lose their health insurance because of Dan Meuser's votes. Rachel will fight to fix the damage done by Dan, save our rural hospitals; end the practice of prior authorization.

priorities.text: Says she is focused on lowering the cost of living, from electricity prices to housing to groceries, and on bringing people together to solve local problems.
Lists health care, cost of living, data centers, housing, veterans, farmers, infrastructure, and jobs as the policy areas she is most passionate about.

positions.summary: Supports capping the share of insurance premiums that can go to insurance-company salaries and ending prior-authorization requirements; opposes coverage losses she attributes to Meuser's votes.
positions.quote: end the practice of prior authorization, which lets insurance companies off the hook for covering services they promise to cover; and cap the amount of insurance premiums that can go to insurance company salaries

candidates.researchNotes: No prior elected office found; a personal campaign website was not located within the research budget, so priorities and positions are drawn from her Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response.
